agent_primer:
Logic Pro is Apple's professional digital audio workstation (DAW) for recording, editing, mixing, and producing music. It is macOS-only. There is no command-palette equivalent; canonical action surfaces are the top menu bar, single-letter keyboard shortcuts (Logic uses unmodified letter keys aggressively — the Tracks area must have focus, not a text field), the Toolbar, the Inspector, and per-editor hotkeys (Piano Roll, Audio Editor). Most pixel-level state lives in custom views that are largely opaque to the macOS accessibility tree — verification on Logic Pro should default to `interpret_check` (vision) for anything that affects waveforms, MIDI notes, mixer state, or playhead position, and to `file_check` for anything that bounces or writes to disk. v0 is macOS-only because Logic Pro itself is macOS-only.

Key UI elements (default workspace, Logic Pro 11+):

- **Tracks area** (center, the main edit surface): horizontal multi-track timeline. Each row is a **track** (audio, software-instrument, drummer, external-MIDI, or auxiliary). Clips on a track are called **regions** — audio regions are colored waveforms, MIDI regions are colored blocks of note data. The **playhead** is the vertical line that moves during playback. The horizontal axis is time (bars / beats by default; switch to SMPTE in the Display menu).
- **Mixer** (toggled with `X`): bottom panel of channel strips, one per track plus busses / aux / output. Each strip has Insert slots (effects), Send slots (aux routing), pan, fader, mute (`M` while strip selected), solo (`S`), and input/output assignment. The Mixer is a separate window state — toggling it shows / hides the panel; it does not occupy a separate window unless detached.
- **Library** (left, toggled with `Y`): patches, instrument presets, channel-strip settings. Selecting a track shows its compatible library entries.
- **Inspector** (left, toggled with `I`): contextual parameter pane for the selected track and selected region. Shows quantize, transposition, region gain, fade in/out, and instrument-specific controls when expanded.
- **Smart Controls** (bottom, toggled with `B`): a hand-curated subset of the most useful parameters for the selected track's instrument and effects — knobs and sliders mapped from buried plugin parameters.
- **Toolbar** (top): common actions (record, count-in toggle, metronome toggle, snap mode, drag mode). Right-clickable to customize.
- **Control Bar** (very top, above Tracks area): transport controls (play / stop / record / cycle), LCD displays for position and tempo, master mute/solo indicators, modes (low-latency, replace).
- **Editors** (bottom or detached): the **Piano Roll** (`P`) edits MIDI note data of the selected MIDI region; the **Audio Editor** edits audio file / region content (Editor button or double-click an audio region); the **Step Editor** does grid-based MIDI; **Score Editor** does notation.

Critical concepts:

- **Tracks vs regions**: a track is a lane on the timeline; a region is a clip on that lane. Most edit operations target a selected region (or selected notes within a region). Track-level operations (mute, solo, freeze, automation lane) target the track header.
- **Playhead**: the current playback position. `space` toggles play / stop. `return` rewinds to the project start. `,` and `.` nudge by transient or beat (depends on snap). `R` toggles record-arm-and-go on the selected track.
- **Locators**: left and right markers that bound the **cycle region** (loop). `C` toggles cycle on/off. The locator span is shown as a yellow / orange bar in the ruler. `cmd+U` sets locators by region selection.
- **Zoom**: `cmd+left/right` zooms time horizontally; `cmd+up/down` zooms track height vertically. `Z` zooms to fit the selection (or whole project if nothing is selected).
- **Takes folders and comping**: when recording in cycle mode over an existing region, Logic stacks each pass into a **takes folder**. Open the folder to comp (combine the best sections across takes).
- **Automation**: per-track automation lanes (toggle with `A`) record parameter moves over time. Modes: Read, Touch, Latch, Write.
- **Flex Time / Flex Pitch**: time-stretch and pitch-shift audio non-destructively. Enabled per track from the track header.
- **Channel strips**: every track has one. Inserts are processed top-to-bottom; sends route a copy to busses.

Bouncing / exporting (writing to disk):

- **File → Bounce → Project or Section… (`cmd+B`)**: render the project (or the cycle region) to an audio file. Opens a modal Bounce dialog with format options (WAV / AIFF / CAF / MP3 / M4A / M4B), bit depth, sample rate, normalize options, dither, and a Bounce button. The bounce includes any **rendering tail** beyond the project end — set the End position generously if you have long reverbs.
- **File → Bounce in Place (`control+B`)**: applies all inserts on a selected region and writes a new audio file in place of the region (replaces with a flattened audio region). Different from Bounce → Project — this acts on a region, not on the master output.
- **File → Export → All Tracks as Audio Files**: stems for sharing with mixing engineers.
- **Save**: `cmd+S` saves the project package (`.logicx` bundle). New projects prompt for a save location on first save.

Rendering tail considerations: bouncing stops at the End position by default. If a reverb or delay tail extends past the last MIDI / audio region, that tail is truncated. Drag the End marker (the right end of the project length bar in the ruler) to extend the bounce window before bouncing.

Keyboard shortcut focus:

- Logic uses single-letter shortcuts (no modifiers) for many common actions. These ONLY fire when the Tracks area has focus — if focus is in a text field (track name rename, search box, parameter input), the letter is typed instead. If a shortcut doesn't seem to do anything, click an empty space in the Tracks area first to restore focus.
- The Key Commands editor (`Logic Pro → Key Commands → Edit…` or `option+K`) is the source of truth for the user's mapping. Custom mappings are common; the seed shortcuts here use Logic's published defaults.

Accessibility-tree caveats: the Tracks area waveform display, Piano Roll, Mixer faders, and most plugin UIs are drawn into custom views and are largely invisible to the macOS AX tree. Use `interpret_check` for any verification of waveform / note / fader / playhead state. File-system writes (bounce) verify cleanly via `file_check`. Modal dialog presence (Save As, Bounce dialog) shows up in the AX tree but the v0 MCP doesn't expose it — interpret_check for modal verification too.

Version notes: this seed targets Logic Pro 11+ (the 2024 release with Session Players and Stem Splitter). Earlier 10.x versions differ on: the Bounce in Place shortcut (was `control+B` from 10.4 onward), Quick Sampler / Drum Machine Designer presence, and the Mixer / Library toggle keys (X / Y are stable since 10.0).
